_source.name: Arkiv: Global Tour Stop 🌍
_source.tagline: A special edition on the road to Devcon 8 Mumbai. Ten days to build on Arkiv, the Web3 database.
_source.desc:
Build on [Arkiv](https://arkiv.network), the Web3 database, around one theme: **CROPS**, the Ethereum Foundation's mandate that Ethereum stay **c**ensorship resistant, **o**pen source, **p**rivate and **s**ecure.

Ten days, fully online, open to builders everywhere. The challenge opens live at Network School Astana during the Network State Conference on **9 October** and closes on **18 October**. Five winners get a Devcon 8 ticket on top of their prize.

Build anything useful and usable for the ecosystem: a dApp, a library, an SDK, a devtool, a CLI, an indexer, a dataset, an agent, a browser extension or more. Four CROPS tracks are open to everyone, and the Best Indian Use Case track rewards a real-world application that people in India can use.

## Prizes

- **Best Indian Use Case:** Devcon 8 ticket + **$2,000 USDC**. A real-world application built on Arkiv that people in India can use. It does not need to follow a CROPS pillar. Your team needs at least one member of Indian nationality.
- **Censorship Resistance (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Open Source (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Privacy (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**
- **Security (Global):** Devcon 8 ticket + **$750 USDC**

### Prize conditions

- **One prize per team.** You can enter more than one track, but your team wins at most one prize. If you win Best Indian Use Case, you cannot also win a Global prize. If you win one Global prize, you cannot win another.
- **Attending Devcon is not required to win.**
- **One Devcon ticket per winning team.** Travel, visa and accommodation are the winner's cost.
- Winners accept their prize within 48 hours and complete KYC. Prizes are paid within 14 days after KYC.

## Dates

All times are London time (BST, UTC+1).

- **7 October:** registration opens
- **9 October, 12:00:** opening, live at Network School Astana
- **18 October, 23:59 (22:59 UTC):** submissions close
- **19 to 22 October:** judging. Keep your deployment up.
- **23 October:** winners announced
- **25 October:** deadline for winners to accept their prize
- **3 to 6 November:** Devcon 8, Mumbai

## How it is judged

Pick **one or more tracks** when you submit: the four CROPS pillars and Best Indian Use Case. All projects are scored on four criteria, 25 points each. The first one depends on the track and is scored for each track you enter:

- **Why this pillar?** (CROPS tracks) Who is harmed today if this data is censored, shut down, leaked or forged?
- **Why India?** (Best Indian Use Case) Who in India uses it, and what real problem does it solve for them?
- **Why Arkiv?** What would break on Postgres, IPFS, a subgraph or your own API, and what did you keep off Arkiv on purpose?
- **How you use Arkiv:** how and why you use each Arkiv feature. Not how many you use.
- **Friction report:** specific, reproducible feedback on building with Arkiv.

Before scoring, every project must pass the gates: a public deployment judges can open without asking for access (libraries, CLIs and datasets too), reproducible steps, a public MIT repo, `/arkiv/schema.md`, `/arkiv/friction.md`, the wallet addresses that create your Arkiv entities on Tiramisu, a demo video of 3 minutes or less, every required question on the submission form answered, and work built between 9 and 18 October. Disclose any pre-existing work with its baseline commit SHA. A project needs at least 50/100 to win.

**Disqualified:** plagiarised work; no meaningful Arkiv use (SDK installed but never queried, or a conventional database app with Arkiv branding); private keys, secrets or real personal data stored in Arkiv, in plaintext or hashed (use synthetic data); malicious code; no working app; late entries. At the deadline we record your repo's commit SHA and judge that commit. Rewriting history after the deadline disqualifies the entry. Keep your deployment up until 23 October.

## Build on Tiramisu

- **Network:** Tiramisu testnet, chain ID `7738577`
- **HTTP RPC:** `https://rpc.tiramisu.db-chain.testnet.arkiv.network`
- **WebSocket RPC:** `wss://rpc.tiramisu.db-chain.testnet.arkiv.network`
- **Explorer:** [tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network](https://tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network)
- **SDK:** [`@arkiv-network/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@arkiv-network/sdk) 0.8.x
- **Docs:** [docs.arkiv.network](https://docs.arkiv.network/networks/tiramisu/)
- **Arkiv Hub** [hub.arkiv.network/](https://hub.arkiv.network/)

## Rules

The full rules, rubric and submission checklist live in [Arkiv-Network/global-tour-stop-pre-devcon](https://github.com/Arkiv-Network/global-tour-stop-pre-devcon). That repo is the only canonical source: if anything here differs, the repo applies.

Questions: [Arkiv Discord](https://discord.gg/arkiv).

_source.name: BIOS V2
_source.tagline: A hackathon where life and computation meet
_source.location: Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology, Bhadson Road, Adarsh Nagar, Prem Nagar, Patiala, Punjab, India
_source.desc:
In a computer, the **BIOS** is the first thing that runs. Here, it's the first point of contact, where life and computation begin speaking to each other.

**BIOS V2** is CSED's flagship hackathon, run with the **IEEE Student Chapter** at **Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, Patiala**. It brings **300 shortlisted builders in 60 teams** to campus for **48 hours of building**, from **30 October to 1 November 2026**.

---

## Pick Your Track

### SEED: School Students (Grades 9 to 12)
Problem statements for school students, solved on campus. Seed has two routes:

- **Idea Lab:** for students strongest in research, design and problem solving. Ends in an **evidence-led proposal or low-fidelity prototype** and a **live pitch**.
- **Build Lab:** a supervised build that ends in a **working prototype** and a **technical defence**.

*Both routes get their own stage time and awards.*

### CORE: College Students
Problem statements set at a **more approachable level**. The right starting point for **emerging builders**.

### FRONTIER: College Students
The **hardest problem statements at BIOS**, built for **advanced AI, systems and research work**. Expect **demanding evaluation** and **live technical questioning**.

### FORGE: Industry Partnerships
**Companies write the problem statements**, and screened teams build on them. Teams that perform well get the chance at **2-month and 6-month internships** with the partner company.

---

Expect **AI agents, coding tools and multimodal apps**, with the freedom to **compare and switch models** as you build.

---

## Team Rules

- **Every team must have exactly 4 members.**
- **Every team must include at least 1 female member.** Teams without one will not qualify.

---

## Prizes: $240,000+ (₹2,27,00,000+)

**Cash prizes, platform credits, tools and perks**, with something for the teams that ship.

---

### **Ship something that works. Defend it on stage.**

**Venue:** Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology, Patiala
**Dates:** 30 Oct to 1 Nov 2026
**Website:** [bios.notyouraverage.xyz](https://bios.notyouraverage.xyz/)

Ten years ago, Hackman began at DSCE, bringing students together to build, experiment, and turn their ideas into projects. Today, it stands as the oldest hackathon at DSCE and one of the oldest student hackathons in Bengaluru. Now, as we return for our **10th edition**, we're excited to celebrate a decade of Hackman with all of you!

Organised by **GENESIS**, the student club of the Department of Information Science & Engineering at Dayananda Sagar College of Engineering, Hackman X is a **24-hour offline hackathon** happening at the DSCE campus.

Got an idea you've been waiting to work on? Want to try something you've never built before? Or just want to spend 24 hours coding, figuring things out with your team, and turning an idea into something real? This is your chance!

- **Cash prizes and more!** Compete for cash prizes and exciting rewards from our sponsors.
- **Render credits:** All attendees can claim $50 in Render building credits through a dedicated link we'll share during the hackathon.
- **A domain of your own:** Every member of the teams selected for the final offline round will receive a .xyz domain.
- **Mentorship:** Get guidance from mentors and industry professionals as you work on your project.
- **New connections:** Meet fellow builders, exchange ideas, and find people who are just as excited about tech as you are.

And of course, you get to be part of **Hackman's 10th edition**, a milestone we're genuinely excited to celebrate!

## Ready to join us?

Get your team together, start thinking about what you want to build, and send in your application. We can't wait to see what you come up with!

# Welcome to the epicentre of innovation and collaboration – the D4 Community's Hackathon at Chandigarh University!

**What We Are:**
D4 Community is proud to present an exciting **one-day hackathon hosted at Chandigarh University**, bringing together undergraduate students, budding tech enthusiasts, aspiring innovators, and problem solvers under one roof.

This hackathon is all about **building ideas into working products using Vibe Coding and Antigravity**. Instead of spending hours worrying about every line of code, participants can focus on their ideas, creativity, experimentation, and problem-solving while using AI-powered development to bring their vision to life.

**Who can join**
Only for **undergraduate students**.

**Individual Participation Only** — this is a solo hackathon. Every participant will ideate, build, and present their own project.

> **Important Note:** This is an **individual participation hackathon**. On the registration platform, you may see an option to add up to **4 participants**. Please ignore this and register as an individual participant. Due to platform restrictions, we are currently unable to change the maximum participant limit from 4 to 1.

**Our Mission:**
Our mission is simple yet profound: to challenge participants to take an idea and turn it into something real within a single day.

With **Vibe Coding using Antigravity**, participants can experiment with AI-assisted development, iterate quickly, and transform their ideas into functional prototypes.

The focus isn't on how much code you can write. It's about **what you can imagine, how you solve problems, and what you can build.**

**What to Expect:**
Expect an action-packed **one day of ideation, vibe coding, experimentation, and building**.

Participants will:

* Build individually from idea to prototype.
* Explore **Vibe Coding with Antigravity**.
* Use AI-assisted development to accelerate their workflow.
* Turn ideas into functional applications and prototypes.
* Experiment, iterate, break things, and build again.
* Solve interesting real-world or everyday problems.
* Present their final projects at the end of the hackathon.
* Connect with fellow builders, mentors, and tech enthusiasts.

You don't need to spend the entire day writing code line by line.

**Bring an idea. Bring your creativity. Bring your curiosity. Let Antigravity handle the building with you.**

**Hackathon Themes:**

> **Health & Wellness** : Build solutions that make healthcare, wellness, fitness, or everyday well-being simpler, smarter, and more accessible.

> **Education & Learning** : Create products that improve the way people learn, teach, practice, collaborate, or access educational resources.

> **Productivity & Lifestyle** : Build tools that help people manage their time, work, tasks, routines, finances, or everyday activities more effectively.

> **Social Impact** : Use technology to address problems faced by communities, individuals, or society and create solutions that can make a meaningful difference.

> **Business & Innovation** : Build innovative products, platforms, or tools that solve business problems, improve existing experiences, or create new opportunities.

> **Entertainment & Creativity** : Build something fun, interactive, creative, or completely unexpected. Explore new ways to entertain, create, and engage.

> **Open Theme** : Have an idea that doesn't fit into any of the above? That's completely fine. Build **anything you want**. If you can imagine it, you can build it.

**Why Join Us:**
Join us to experience a completely different way of building products.

Sharpen your problem-solving skills, experiment with **Vibe Coding**, learn how to work with AI-assisted development, and turn an idea into a working prototype — **all in a single day.**

Whether you're already familiar with AI-powered development or you're trying it for the first time, this hackathon is an opportunity to **learn by building**.

No team. No waiting for teammates. No complicated setup.

**Just you, your idea, Antigravity, and one day to build.**

**Stay Tuned:**
Stay tuned for updates, registration details, rules, judging criteria, and exciting announcements as we gear up for an unforgettable hackathon experience.

Get ready to experiment with **Vibe Coding**, explore what you can build with **Antigravity**, and turn your ideas into reality.

**Mark your calendars and get ready to build with D4 Community's One-Day Vibe Coding Hackathon at Chandigarh University!**

_source.desc:
HAXFINITY — Hack the Infinite

The 24-hour hackathon of XTHRON '26

 December 2026
Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala
Prize Pool: Exciting prizes
Team Size: 2–4 participants

Build real solutions. Solve meaningful problems. Create something that works.

HAXFINITY is the 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON '26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur.

For 24 hours, students from different colleges and backgrounds will come together to identify problems, develop  software solutions, build working prototypes, and present their ideas to a panel of judges.

There is no compulsory theme. Participants are free to choose a problem and develop a software solution using any suitable technology.

Whether you are an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, HAXFINITY is a space to learn, collaborate, experiment, and build.

PRIZE POOL — Exciting prizes


TRACKS

OPEN INNOVATION

Build anything that solves a real problem.

You may work in education, healthcare, finance, agriculture, entertainment, productivity, cybersecurity, accessibility, sustainability, or any other domain.

There is no fixed problem statement and no restriction on technology. Choose a problem, design a solution, build a working prototype, and surprise the judges.

AI / ML

Build intelligent systems using machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, recommendation systems, data analysis, or any other AI-related technology.

Projects will be evaluated on technical implementation, originality, usefulness, and real-world applicability.

SOCIAL GOOD

Build technology that improves people’s lives.

Possible areas include rural development, accessibility, mental health, financial inclusion, education, healthcare, environmental protection, and community welfare.

Projects in this track will be evaluated on impact, usability, sustainability, and the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

WHAT THE HACKATHON LOOKS LIKE

12 December, 10:30 AM — Opening ceremony and problem-solving begins.

During the day — Teams form, ideas take shape, and development begins.

Throughout the event — Mentoring, technical support, checkpoints, and interaction with fellow participants.

Midnight — The hackathon continues with snacks, discussions, debugging, and late-night building.

13 December, 10:32 AM — Submission deadline and code freeze.

After submission — Teams prepare their final demonstrations.

Final judging — Each team presents its working prototype to the judges.

Closing ceremony — Winners are announced and prizes are distributed.

WHO CAN PARTICIPATE?

HAXFINITY is open to students from all streams and colleges.

Students from computer science, information technology, engineering, science, commerce, management, design, and other disciplines are welcome.

You may participate if you are:

- A beginner attending your first hackathon.
- An experienced developer.
- A designer or creative problem-solver.
- A student interested in AI, cybersecurity, cloud, web, mobile, or social-impact technology.
- Someone with an idea and the willingness to build it.

The only requirement is that you come prepared to learn, collaborate, and create.

TEAM DETAILS

- Each team must have 2–4 participants.
- Solo participation is not permitted.
- Participants from different colleges may form one team.
- Participants from different academic streams may form one team.
- Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.
- Each participant may be part of only one team.

WHERE IT HAPPENS

Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)
Santhigramam, Eranhimangad
Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329

The campus is located in the Nilambur region of Kerala, known for its natural surroundings and teak forests.

The college is approximately:

- 3 km from Nilambur Railway Station.
- 1 km from the Calicut–Nilambur–Ooty highway.

Travel and accommodation information will be shared with registered participants.

WHAT WE PROVIDE

- Dedicated workspace for participating teams.
- Power and internet access.
- Lunch on the first day.
- Dinner on the first day.
- Breakfast on the second day.
- Midnight snacks.
- Technical assistance during the event.
- Mentoring and guidance, subject to mentor availability.
- Certificates for participants.
- A platform to demonstrate projects to judges and fellow innovators.

Cloud credits, software benefits, and additional resources may be announced later if they are officially confirmed.

RULES

- Teams must contain 2–4 participants.
- The project must be developed during the official hackathon period.
- Participants may use open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and publicly available datasets.
- Previously developed projects may not be submitted as new work.
- Teams must clearly disclose any pre-existing code, templates, datasets, APIs, or third-party services used.
- Projects must be submitted through Devfolio before the deadline.
- Late submissions may not be accepted.
- A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected.
- Teams must be prepared to explain their technology, development process, and contribution.
- Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law.
- All participants must follow the event Code of Conduct.
- The organisers reserve the right to reject projects that are unsafe, copied, offensive, illegal, or unrelated to the event.
- The detailed judging criteria and final rules will be published before the event.




HAXFINITY — Hack the Infinite
EXTHRONE ’26
12–13 December 2026

hackathon_faqs.question: Is there any registration fee to participate in GeNarrative Clash?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **No, participation is completely free!** There are no entry fees or hidden costs to register, build, or compete in the hackathon.

hackathon_faqs.question: Who can participate? Is the hackathon open to working professionals?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **GeNarrative Clash** is exclusively for currently enrolled university and college students. Working professionals are not eligible to compete as participants, though they are **welcome to join us as mentors or judges.**

hackathon_faqs.question: Do I need to be a Computer Science student to participate?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **Not at all!** Since this hackathon merges Generative AI with the creative arts, we strongly encourage students from design, media, literature, and other non-technical backgrounds to form teams with developers. **Diverse perspectives build the best tools.**

hackathon_faqs.question: Can our team have members from different colleges or universities?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **Yes, Cross-college and inter-disciplinary teams are absolutely allowed.** As long as every member is a currently enrolled student, you can team up with anyone you want.

hackathon_faqs.question: What is the allowed team size?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Teams can consist of anywhere from **2 to 4 members**. We highly recommend having a mix of technical developers and creative designers on your squad.

hackathon_faqs.question: Is the hackathon held entirely online or in person?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **It is a hybrid event.** The first round is online, where you will build and submit your 50% project prototype in between November 10th to November 16th . **The top 150** shortlisted teams will then be invited to Techno India University, Kolkata, on November 21st for the offline 6-hour hack sprint and live final pitches.

hackathon_faqs.question: What exactly do we need to submit for the online evaluation round?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Your online submission must include a **GitHub repository link** demonstrating at least 50% code completion, a clean and **comprehensive README file** explaining your tool, and a **live video demonstration link** showing your working prototype in action.

hackathon_faqs.question: What should we bring if our team is shortlisted for the in-person finale?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Bring your laptops, chargers, any specialized hardware you need, and a valid **college student ID card**. We will provide the **workspace, power outlets, Wi-Fi, and an AI masterclass to kick off the day.**

# GeNarrative Clash 2026
*Where Generative AI Meets Human Creativity*

Are you ready to redefine how stories are told, music is composed, and digital art is created? **GeNarrative Clash** is Kolkata's premier Prompt Engineering & AI Building Challenge, organized by the GeeksforGeeks Student Chapter at Techno India University.

---

### 🚀 Hands-On AI & API Masterclass (Included!)
Don't worry if you are new to AI development! Before the live challenge kicks off, every participant gets access to an exclusive **1-Hour Hands-On Masterclass on AI Development & API Integration**. Learn how to harness cutting-edge LLMs, query GenAI APIs, and leverage rapid prototyping tools so you can build a solid, production-ready product with confidence.

---

### 🎁 Perks, Bounties & Swag
* **Cash Bounties & Prize Pool:** Generous rewards or prizes for top-performing teams and winners.
* **Exclusive Swags:** Official sponsor goodies for top 12 finalists.
* **Certificates for All:** Official certificates of participation and achievement for all attending hackers.

---

### 🎨 The Challenge: Empowering the Creative Artist (Open Track)
Generative AI shouldn't replace human creators, it should supercharge them! **GeNarrative Clash** features an Open Track focused on building real-world solutions that assist, elevate, and support creative artists in their work. 

You are free to solve any real-world problem in the artistic or creative domain.

**Inspiration & Potential Project Directions:**
* **Storytelling & Narrative Assistants:** GenAI co-writers that help authors outline complex multiverses, generate dynamic dialogue, or build interactive narratives.
* **AI Music & Sound Studios:** Production-ready suites that assist musicians with harmonies, stem generation, or intelligent sound design.
* **Autonomous Creator Agents:** GenAI agents and social media co-pilots that help digital creators manage, format, and schedule content tailored to their target audience.
* **Digital Art & Visual Co-Pilots:** Tools that aid animators, illustrators, and designers in concept generation and workflow automation.

---

### ⚙️ Hackathon Rules & Technical Freedom
* **No Tech Stack Restrictions:** You are completely free to use any programming language, framework, API, or LLM (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, or open-source models).
* **The 50/50 Pre-Building Rule:** To ensure high-quality, production-ready submissions, teams are permitted to pre-build up to **50% of their project before event day** (wireframes, boilerplate code, trained prompts, or baseline UI). The remaining **50% of the project must be built live** during the 6-hour hacking sprint.

---

### 📍 Venue & Event Date
* **Date:** November 21, 2026  
* **Venue:** Techno India University, EM Block, Sector V, Salt Lake, Kolkata, West Bengal 700091
